answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents mint unique identities via cryptographic attestation chains verified through zero-knowledge proofs. Valid agents anchor their reputation in a decentralized grove, where each identity branch requires an escalating stake. A malicious swarm attempting to cast a plume of fabricated nodes faces an exponential capital exhaustion curve, making the cost superlinear. Like tracing a rare pigment, verification exposes duplicate computational origins, bankrupting attackers who deploy synthetic swarms.
